W: Pigeonholes, floor to ceiling, stuffed with letters. Some are addressed to people who have been dead for centuries. Nobody throws them away.
Q: The notice board. Year 500's news, pinned in layers:
"BY ORDER OF THE KING: all iron to be surrendered." Underneath, in pencil: "generous."
"LOST: one goose. Answers to Duchess. Do not approach."
"COURIERS WANTED. Must be fast. Must not read the post."
A newer notice, printed, not written. Nobody here owns a press:
"THE EIGHT THANK YOU FOR YOUR REST. NOTHING FURTHER IS REQUIRED OF YOU." Underneath, in pencil: "noted."
c: A candle that burns without shrinking, like the ones in the Archive.
D: The counter. A ledger lies open: every traveller who's rested here, in a hundred different hands.
Near the very first page, in faded ink: a name, scratched out so hard the page has torn.
p: A sack of undelivered post. The oldest letter's seal has a running boot pressed into it.
_: Worn flagstones. Generations of boots have polished a path to the door.

objects.name: Hesper
lines: Welcome to the Waystation! Rest your feet. Candle's free, soup's not.
Two coppers. Three if you sniff it first.

answer: The old couriers' rest. Couriers ran post between every kingdom, once. Fastest people alive.
Now it's mostly me, the soup, and Pell over there dreaming about the old days.
The king in the east names everything after himself. Kaldor Square. Kaldor Street. I hear there's a Kaldor Street that crosses Kaldor Street.
I hear a lot of things. The soup's quiet, so I listen.
The old fort in the hill first, then the Kingdom. The fort's the only way past the king's checkpoints these days.
Mind the fort. And mind the Kingdom. And mind your manners. That's three minds; you'll need them.
Nobody. It was just there one morning, pinned up neat as you like.
They turn up in every town, I hear. Same words. Nobody's ever seen who brings them.

objects.name: Pell
lines: Are you a courier? You walk like a courier. Couriers are the best.
I'm in training. Mostly I run to the well and back. Nine seconds! Nearly.

answer: The fastest who ever lived! Nobody knows her name any more. She ran the last message of the old world.
They say she never delivered it. They say she's still out there somewhere, with the letter, still sealed.
That's the kind of courier I want to be. Except the delivering part. I'd do the delivering part.
There's a gap in the trees behind the signpost. I found it chasing a squirrel.
There's something in there. I didn't take it. Couriers don't take things.
Because one day someone's going to need a message carried, and it's going to matter, and I'm going to be fast enough.
You have to be ready before the day comes. That's the whole trick.

lines: Eight seconds! EIGHT! To the well and back!
Bo taught me to cartwheel the last bit. Don't tell Hesper. She'll charge for the well.

objects.name: Quill
lines: Oh! Oh, you're real! I've read about you. Well, not you. People like you. Travellers.
Quill. Mage. I came in for one book five hundred years ago and I'm still on the index.
